authoredPrompt: This figure is part of a worked example that evaluates the line integral of F = cos(x) i + sin(x) j along two different oriented curves. The figure contains two panels (a) and (b), each showing the same vector field F drawn over a green-shaded background with the note Vectors not to scale. Panel (a): the oriented curve C is a short vertical red line segment at x = -pi/2, directed downards from y = 2 to y = 1. Panel (b): the oriented curve C is a parabolic arc from (-1, 1) to (2, 4), directed first down, then upward and to the right. The figure shows the two distinct integration paths for parts (a) and (b) of the example, making visible how each curve's geometry and alignment relative to the field vectors determines the computed line integral. Note that the two parts of the image are differently scaled.
authoredInteractions:
- Drag the endpoints of curve C to reshape the integration path through the vector field and watch the line integral value update in real time
- Toggle between the two panels (short vertical path vs. long curved path) to compare how path shape and length affect the line integral value over the same field
- Slider for parameter t: animate a moving point along C and display the field vector and its dot product with the tangent at each step

discrepancies: The 'Vectors not to scale' caption is drawn inside the plot at the top edge where it collides with the y-axis arrowhead and 'y' label, rather than sitting as a clear title above the panel as in the source

The blue F vector and green tangent vector at r(t) are extra overlays not in the source; on the narrow vertical segment of panel (a) they stack directly on top of the red curve and its endpoints, cluttering the exact region the source keeps clean

In the source the field arrows are noticeably longer relative to grid spacing and more densely varied in direction; the generated arrows are shorter and sparser, making the field pattern (e.g. the near-vertical band around x = −π/2) less visually striking

The source panel (a) shows the segment endpoints at y = 1 and y = 2 with the 'C' label to the right of the segment midpoint; the generated 'C' label sits close to the moving r(t) marker and overlays rather than beside the curve
evaluation.notes: Both panels of the source are correctly implemented behind a working A/B toggle with the right field F = cos(x)i + sin(x)j, correct paths, and a rich, functional t-slider/animation/drag interaction with a live line-integral readout; the main weaknesses are the title colliding with the y-axis label and the overlaid F/tangent arrows cluttering the curve in panel (a).
action_items: Move 'Vectors not to scale' above the plot area (or shift the y-axis label) so it no longer overlaps the axis arrowhead and 'y' label
Anchor the 'C' label at a fixed offset from the curve midpoint rather than near the moving r(t) marker so it does not drift or overlap the marker
Reduce the length of the blue F and green tangent arrows (or offset their tails from r(t)) so they don't stack on top of the red curve and endpoints on the narrow vertical segment
Increase field arrow length/density slightly to better match the source's bolder vector-field look
